title: Endocrine mechanisms in the sarcopenia model following distal radius fracture
summary:
This research aims to better understand sarcopenia, a condition in which muscle mass and strength decrease with age. The study will focus on patients with a wrist fracture to explore how reduced activity and recovery affect muscle health.
MRI scans will be used to assess muscle loss and fat accumulation in the muscles. These findings will be compared with bone health, muscle strength, and physical function, as well as with blood markers related to muscle health, especially the hormone IGF-I.
The goal is to make MRI a practical tool for diagnosing and predicting sarcopenia in everyday care and to support better treatment planning for older patients by combining imaging results with blood test information.
conditions: Muscle wasting and atrophy, not elsewhere classified: multiple locations

interventions.name: Diagnosis of a distal radius fracture with indication for conservative treatment. All patients > 50 years of age are included in the study, both genders are considered.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Diagnosis of a distal radius fracture with indication for conservative treatment. All patients > 50 years of age are included in the study, both genders are considered.
Exclusion criteria:
Contraindications for performing an MRI.
